subject: Ramber SLO onboarding & customer-led load test — next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ramber.ai>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@ramber.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Ramber SLO onboarding & customer-led load test — next steps

Hi Samir / Priya — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same playbook: 

- Target SLOs you confirmed: 95th latency <= 350ms for inference (non-streaming) and sustained streaming concurrency of 60 concurrent clients with 99th percentile response <= 700ms.
- Desired throughput for the customer-led run: 750–1,000 RPS burst capacity to 1.2k for a 10m ramp window.
- Test tooling: you indicated a preference to run customer-led k6 scripts (we also support Locust if you prefer).

To keep the run smooth, can you share the following by EOD Tuesday: 
1) k6 script (or Locust) you plan to use (we can validate locally).
2) Test account email(s) you want us to allowlist (we'll provision a dedicated staging key).
3) Proposed test windows (we suggest two options, so we can coordinate capacity).
4) Any special payload shapes (token lengths, streaming vs non-streaming mix).

I've attached an initial SLO playbook that outlines our preflight checklist and recommended ramp pattern. Evelyn, Rachel — can you confirm the allowlist IP ranges and a preflight slot for Wed?

Attachments: ramber_slo_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook & ramp template)

Thanks — happy to hop on 15m if you want to walk the playbook.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191
https://redwood.ai
From: Samir Patel <samir@ramber.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@ramber.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ramber SLO onboarding & customer-led load test — next steps

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming items below and attaching our k6 script (mini payloads for initial run).

Quick answers:
- We'll run k6 (script attached: ramber_k6_script_v2.js). Primary target: 900 RPS sustained, 10m steady-state, with 5m ramp up/down.
- Test accounts: test+load@ramber.ai and qa+load@ramber.ai (we'll use the staging key you provision).
- Windows: Option A — Thu Dec 3, 10:00–11:30 PST. Option B — Fri Dec 4, 02:00–03:30 PST (backup).
- Payload shapes: mostly short prompts (avg 40 tokens) with a small subset (~10%) long context (400–800 tokens) to exercise KV cache.

Attachments: ramber_k6_script_v2.js (k6 script), sample_payloads.json (small), ramber_test_account_creds.txt (placeholder).

On the stream requirement: we can start non-streaming runs first to validate baseline latency; if that looks good we will run a separate streaming concurrency rehearsal.

On Tue we'll also share a short benchmark trace from our side (to compare token distribution).

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Performance Engineering, Ramber
samir@ramber.ai | +1 (650) 555-2244
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ramber.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@ramber.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ramber SLO onboarding & customer-led load test — next steps

Thanks Samir — received the script and payloads. A couple of operational notes from our side (preflight):

- IP allowlist: please allow these egress IP ranges for the run: 34.82.120.0/24, 35.199.12.0/24, 52.34.168.0/24. We'll also add the test account emails to our staging allowlist.
- Test API key: I'll provision a short-lived staging key bound to the test accounts and send it via a secure link (DocuSign/Drive private share).
- Preflight slot: Wed Dec 2, 15:00–15:30 PST — this is a validation-only window (no heavy load). Please confirm who will join from Ramber for the preflight.
- Ramp pattern we recommend for the customer-led run: 5m linear ramp to 600 RPS, 5m linear ramp to 900 RPS hold 10m, then 5m linear ramp down. We prefer starting with non-streaming to validate token path.

I've attached our preflight checklist and a short checklist of telemetry to capture (traces, p50/p95/p99 latencies, token-level billing samples). Also note one constraint: if we see sustained p99 > 1.2s during validation we'll automatically step down to a lower concurrency and rerun (we'll notify immediately).

Attachments: preflight-checklist.xlsx

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0110
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ramber.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@ramber.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ramber SLO onboarding & customer-led load test — next steps

Appreciate the clarity, Evelyn. Samir / Priya — a couple of follow-ups before the preflight: 

- Fallback model variant: do you want an aggressive fallback to a smaller quantized model if latency exceeds SLO, or a graceful degradation policy (reduce concurrency first)? We can configure either; recommendation is to reduce concurrency for a single run and trigger fallback only if user-facing errors occur.
- KV/cache warm-up: for the long-context subset, do you want us to pre-warm KV caches using a synthetic pass prior to the steady-state hold? That reduces tail variance.
- Success criteria for the non-streaming run: p95 <= 350ms and p99 <= 1.0s for the steady-state window. Please confirm so we can mark run as SLO pass/fail automatically.

If everything looks good I'll schedule the preflight slot and share the secure staging key link. Also tagging Rachel to confirm billing/unit expectations for the test window (short-lived keys and promo credits).

— Alex
From: Priya Nair <priya.nair@ramber.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@ramber.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ramber SLO onboarding & customer-led load test — next steps

Thanks everyone — short answers inline: 

> fallback model variant: do you want an aggressive fallback to a smaller quantized model if latency exceeds SLO, or a graceful degradation policy?
We prefer graceful degradation first (reduce concurrency by 20%) and only fall back to a smaller model if we see errors or user-impacting quality loss.

> KV/cache warm-up: for the long-context subset, do you want us to pre-warm KV caches?
Yes please — pre-warm pass prior to steady-state. We'll include warmup iterations in the k6 script if you want (we can send a minor update).

> Success criteria for the non-streaming run: p95 <= 350ms and p99 <= 1.0s
Confirmed. We'll aim to hit those thresholds.

We'll be on the preflight slot Wed Dec 2, 15:00 PST — Samir and I will join. Rachel — if you can confirm the test credits/short-lived key and add the allowlist IPs, we can proceed.

Regards,
Priya Nair
Director, DevOps, Ramber
priya.nair@ramber.ai
